class.name: NNBTSelector
class.brief_description: Executes its child nodes from top-to-bottom order until one of them succeeds (returning [code]1[/code]) or all of them fail (returning [code]-1[/code]).
class.description: This node type is used to create fallbacks. The [NNBTSelector] node executes its child nodes from top-to-bottom order until one of them succeeds (returning [code]1[/code]) or all of them fail (returning [code]-1[/code]). If a child returns running (0) the selector will return running to its parent. The [NNBTRandomSelector] works similarly, it just shuffles the nodes into a random order before ticking them. By default the selector resumes from the child that was running on the previous tick. When [member reactive] is [code]true[/code] the selector instead starts evaluating at child 0 on every tick, so the highest-priority branch is re-checked while a lower-priority branch is running. In both modes disabled children are skipped and a child that returns [code]SKIP[/code] is skipped over, so the selector continues with the next child. Reactive evaluation is independent of [code]reset_rule[/code]: it only changes the starting child index.

members.member: When [code]true[/code], every tick starts evaluating at child 0 instead of resuming from the previously running child. Disabled children are skipped and a [code]SKIP[/code] result makes the selector continue with the next child. This is independent of [code]reset_rule[/code].
